light.notes: bg base2, paper base3, chip base2 (the palette has two light tones); border derived (base2 toward base1); text-1 base01 emphasised, text-2 base00 body, text-3 base1; amber is orange, purple is violet, series two is cyan and four is magenta

dark.notes: bg base03, paper base02, chip base02; border derived (base02 toward base01); text-1 base1, text-2 base0, text-3 base01. The palette has one value per accent. red, orange, and violet are lifted a few points of lightness (52% to 58%, 44% to 48%, 60% to 63%) to meet 3:1 as text on base02 (MAD-372). blue is lifted from 49% to 53% so base03 ink reads 4.5 on it (MAD-376). The roles derived from the four stay pinned to the published values. A fill light enough to read on base02 is too light for white ink at 4.5. base03 ink needs a fill at luminance 0.265, which red, orange, and violet reach only by leaving the published hues. So those three stay under 4.5: the ink rule keeps white on red and orange, at 4.0 against base03's 3.8, and takes base03 on violet, at 3.9 against white's 3.8
